items.notes: Quote: "_urllib3_request_context (adapters.py:95) hands that connection the single module-level _preloaded_ssl_context; urllib3 (2.8.0) then calls context.load_cert_chain() directly on it, with no copy, permanently embedding the client cert in the shared singleton." GT-i1's shared-mutation manifestation, mechanism correct (urllib3 util/ssl_.py:431). Fix: "In cert_verify ... set conn.ssl_context = None before assigning conn.cert_file/conn.key_file". As written this is ineffective: conn in cert_verify is the HTTPSConnectionPool, and urllib3 2.8.0 passes the context to connections only via **self.conn_kw (connectionpool.py:1099-1114), never a pool attribute ssl_context, so the shared context would still be used; it also does nothing for the override manifestation. Graded partial (a change is proposed, but it restores at most the intent for one manifestation, and not as written).

Quote: "No test in the suite exercises _urllib3_request_context or _preloaded_ssl_context directly". Verified: grep of tests/ for both names returns no hits. A test-coverage observation with no defect of its own.

Quote: "A subclass overrides send() to call the older, still-public self.get_connection(url, proxies) ... then calls self.cert_verify(conn, url, True, cert)"; "The resulting pool has cert_reqs='CERT_REQUIRED' but ca_certs=None ... urllib3's ssl_wrap_socket() then falls back to ssl.SSLContext.load_default_certs() (the OS trust store) instead of requests' pinned certifi bundle". This is exactly GT-i3 manifestation (b): cert_verify no longer supplies certifi for verify=True (diff removes conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)), so get_connection pools verify against the OS store. Clears the bar. Fix is partial: it proposes `conn.ssl_context = _preloaded_ssl_context` in cert_verify, but conn is an HTTPSConnectionPool and urllib3 2.8.0 reads ssl_context only from pool.conn_kw (connectionpool.py:1099-1114 _new_conn passes **self.conn_kw; no self.ssl_context), so the assignment as written would not reach connections; it also does not cover the HTTPS-proxy TLS leg (ca_certs-based) or reset a stale ca_certs left by an earlier verify=<path> call (and if it did take effect, a stale ca_certs would be loaded into the shared context). 'Failing every HTTPS request through that adapter' overstates the general case but is stated for the no-OS-store environment.

Quote: "_urllib3_request_context() hands out the single module-level _preloaded_ssl_context to every verify=True pool, cert or not. urllib3 calls context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile) on whatever ssl_context it's given whenever cert_file is set, so one client-cert request permanently loads that certificate onto the shared object". Same mechanism as GT-i1's shared-mutation manifestation (confirmed in urllib3 2.8.0 util/ssl_.py:431). Fix (stop reusing the shared context when client_cert is set; build or cache per-cert contexts) confines the mutation, but leaves the override manifestation (subclass init_poolmanager ssl_context replaced by _preloaded_ssl_context for verify=True) untouched: partial.

Quote: "_preloaded_ssl_context.load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)) now runs unconditionally at requests.adapters import time, whereas before this change ... only ran lazily". Accurate (diff lines 75-78), but rendered as a bare observation: no consequence (no import-time error or import-cost regression) and no corrective change is asserted, so it only describes GT-i2's placement without identifying the defect a reader would act on. Non-material observation.

Quote: "import requests now unconditionally runs _preloaded_ssl_context.load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)) at module load"; "the bare import now raises an unhandled FileNotFoundError ... succeeds at the merge-base (the check was lazy, inside cert_verify())". This is GT-i2's mechanism with an import-time failure manifestation of the same kind as #6764; true from the diff (lines 75-78 run at import, the merge-base's equivalent sat in cert_verify). Fix: move the create/load pair behind an lru_cache'd function invoked only from the verify-is-True branch, which defers extraction and loading until use and so satisfies the required outcome for both the import-time error and import-cost manifestations: sufficient.

Quote: "it always writes the same CERT_REQUIRED value back ... so it is a redundant write, not an observed defect." The item itself disclaims a defect; the shared context is only placed in pool_kwargs on the verify-is-True branch (diff adapters.py:94-95), where cert_reqs is CERT_REQUIRED. Accurate, inconsequential observation.

Quote: "adapters.py:75-78 builds _preloaded_ssl_context from DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH unconditionally at module import"; "At the merge-base the same lookup ran only inside cert_verify()"; Fix: "Build _preloaded_ssl_context lazily on first verify=True use". This is GT-i2's mechanism (CA-bundle extraction plus load_verify_locations moved from cert_verify()-time to import time, diff lines 75-78) with an import-time failure manifestation of the same class as #6764's import-time PermissionError; a missing bundle making load_verify_locations raise at import is mechanically true from the diff. The primary fix (lazy construction on first verify=True use) meets the required outcome for both known manifestations (import-time error and import cost). The offered alternative (only wrap construction in error handling) would not remove the import-time cost, but the lead proposal is sufficient.

Quote: "_urllib3_request_context's new os.path.isdir(verify) check duplicates the os.path.isdir(cert_loc) check cert_verify() still performs". True (diff adds isdir branch in _urllib3_request_context while cert_verify keeps its own), and the PR author notes the redundancy; it is a redundancy/cleanup remark with no consequence. The register's non-defect says verify=<path> still works.

Quote: "A third local test, test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings, also fails ... unrelated to this diff." Confirmed the test fails at head on this machine (one focused pytest run); its run emits an InsecureRequestWarning, i.e. it exercises the verify=False path, which the diff does not change (register non-defect: verify=False unaffected). An environment observation, not a finding against the change.

Quote: "_urllib3_request_context() puts the same module-level _preloaded_ssl_context object into pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] for every verify=True pool, regardless of client_cert. urllib3's ssl_wrap_socket() calls context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile) on whatever ssl_context object a pool was built with, so loading url_a's client certificate mutates the same context object url_b's ... pool also holds." This is GT-i1's shared-mutation manifestation (register: 'ssl_wrap_socket calls load_cert_chain on the context it is handed, so a client certificate supplied on one thread is loaded into the context every other thread is handshaking with'); confirmed urllib3 2.8.0 util/ssl_.py:431 load_cert_chain on the supplied context. The cross-host client-cert presentation is a direct consequence of that mutation. Fix (do not hand out the shared context when client_cert is set) cures the mutation manifestation but not the override manifestation (a subclass's init_poolmanager ssl_context still overridden by pool_kwargs for verify=True), so partial.

Quote: "The default-CA-bundle SSLContext is now built and loaded at import requests.adapters time ... so this is a deliberate, discussed tradeoff, not a candidate finding." The fact is accurate (diff lines 75-78) and names GT-i2's mechanism, but the item explicitly disclaims it as a defect, names no consequence (import-time PermissionError, import cost) and asks for no change, so a reader would not act on it; it does not recover GT-i2. Recorded as an accurate observation.
